description: The report investigated allegations that the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida (USAO) failed to properly resolve a federal investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's criminal conduct by negotiating a non-prosecution agreement (NPA), thereby deferring prosecution to the State of Florida, as well as allegations of occurrances of professional misconduct in properly informing victims of Epstein's criminal conduct about the NPA prior to and during its signing. The report finds that the Department's attorneys did not engage in professional misconduct, but that U.S. Attorney Alexander Acosta exercised poor judgment in both pursuing the NPA and communicating about it with victims.
headline: U.S. Department of Justice Releases Executive Summary of Report Concerning the Conduct of U.S. Attorney's Office in Its 2006–2008 Investigation

info.description: The Department of Justice's Office of Public Affairs put out a statement that same day, summarizing the summary findings of the report.
info.note: They note that the full text is not available to the public owing to the Privacy Act, but that the Act allows the relevant Congressional Committee to request the full report upon authorized request (which had occurred prior to the public release of the executive summary).
